items.en: You return to the academy concourse.  A junior academy agent - a different one - greets you in a landing lounge with promotional paraphernalia in hand.

"Good."

He turns his attention away, and you see a holographic moon spin past his head.

"I await your return, captain," he says over his shoulder.

"The attached specifications will..." Elek pauses, then squints.

"I see. You're engaging in a bit of jocularity. Well, I can't exactly disapprove of high spirits at the outset of an expedition provided you mind the technical details."

He turns away and begins re-arranging holographic moons that have been floating around him. "I await your return, captain," he says over his shoulder.

"Very well. I'll simply find an adventurer who is interested in the advancement of human knowledge, to say nothing of wealth and glory."

"Good day." He hits the cut-off, and you're left with the logo of the Galatia Academy Planetology Department.
Your $shipOrFleet approaches the $nameInText.

Your operations chief oversees the installation with their usual methodical precision and discipline.

The hardware is interfaced with a secure computing environment on your flagship, and your tech team stands by to oversee the results.

The telemetry streams across space to your flagship by the flicker of the discreet little comms laser your ops team installed.

Your technology officer confirms that while the data isn't perfect, it has a vastly lower corruption rate than Elek's copy from the Galatia Academy archive.

"We have a fix on where they were looking," Tech says proudly as they transfer you the coordinates.

"It would appear to be a minor planet in the Abyss. No star, no nebulae; no primary but itself."

"Well, $playerSirOrMadam, nothing about the rock itself."

"The Domain Explorarium ordered a non-routine survey of the volume. We don't know what they were looking for, but the survey program found... well, it appears as though something happened, something violent. A series of high-energy events over a short period of time a little over 200 cycles ago. A starless rock is, um, very unlikely to produce such effects naturally."

They pause, then speak tentatively. "A battle, maybe? We can't say for sure. I don't know what would be worth fighting over out there. Or even looking for."

There's only one way to find out.

And it's best done with plenty of extra supplies and fuel. Every spacer knows that the Abyss is not to be trifled with. Of those foolish captains who attempt to find their fortune there, the few who return are often starving, having to mothball ships for fuel and supplies during the long crawl back to the Core Worlds.

"$PlayerSirOrMadam," your sensors officer says. "There's a, a large ship in orbit. I mean no presumption, but I think you're going to want to get a closer look. The long-range readings are... unusual."
"Got a long-range hit..." Sensors reports. "Something is approaching our orbit. Without maneuvers we have one shift? Two? Half a day, max."
Academician Elek could not have possibly known his sensor data would lead to... this.
You can only speculate what Tri-Tachyon thought they were setting you up to find using him as a front. It might be nice to find out.
You can only speculate what Director Glamor-Rotanev and Tri-Tachyon thought they were setting you up to find using him as a front. It might be nice to find out.

You can only speculate what his 'patron' thought they were setting you up to find, using him as a front. It might be nice to find out. If you make it out of this alive, a pointed word with Elek about the identity of his patron might be in order.

It's too big, too dangerous for him to have stumbled upon himself. And based on what you know from the sensor array data, it was originally someone elses' project entirely... around 200 cycles ago.

Someone long dead. Probably.

This Academician Elek of the Galatia Academy could not have possibly known his sensor data would lead to... this. Could he?

You might be justified to ask him with an urgency proportional to the magnitude of the situation you now find yourself in.

Only if you manage to survive this 'Threat' and make it back to the Core Worlds, of course.

Your sensors officer finally suppresses the new detector's alerts, then turns to you. The Onslaught Mk.I rotates threateningly in the primary display, an avatar of ancient violence.

"What are your orders, $playerSirOrMadam?" they ask.

Academician Elek could not have possibly known his sensor data would lead to... this. Could he?

It's too big, too dangerous for a pretentious, if bombastic, academic like Elek to have stumbled upon himself. And based on what you know from the sensor array data, it was someone elses' project entirely around 200 cycles ago.

Someone long dead. Probably.

"Greetings! Captain $PlayerName." Academician Elek is as pleased to see you as you've ever seen.

"I trust your expedition was a success. Please, do me the favor of summarizing your findings while you transmit the data you've collected."

He taps at something, and your comms ping softly to notify you that Elek has opened a datastream for you. He looks at you expectantly.
"What?" He lets out an impatient huff. "I already paid you for recovering the data from the sensor array."
Elek raises his eyebrows and gives you a skeptical look.
He lets out an impatient huff.
"Yes, yes, of course. Credits, always about the..." he mutters to himself as he taps and swipes at his datapad.

"Here we are," he says, raising his eyebrows at you. "What I would have paid the other freelancer I hired had they returned. And promptly surrendered the research data that would be useless to anyone but me."

Your TriPad pings softly as Elek gives you a cold look.

"Here we are. The payment."

Your TriPad pings softly.

"Here we are," he says, raising his eyebrows at you.

Your TriPad pings softly.

He lets out a breath, then meets your eyes. "A princely sum. I hope the value of your data will be its equal."

His finger hovers over the confirmation for a full second before he presses it down. Your TriPad pings softly to itself.

He sighs melodramatically, then his eyes meet yours, "This had better be worth it."

His finger hovers over the confirmation for two full seconds before he presses it. Your TriPad pings softly as if it were rather pleased with itself.

"What?" He looks appalled. "Stars above, you spacers... we'll discuss it after I review the data you collected. It is only logical to establish the degree of hazard before I make some potentially spurious additional payment."

"Speaking of precisely that," he taps his datapad impatiently.

Academician Elek seems to pick up on the tone in your voice, for once.

"Yes? Very well, do elaborate." He places his hands together in a well-practiced pose of attentive contemplation.

You tell Elek about finding the sensor array, processing the data, then travelling into the Abyss. Elek nods along, fascinated enough to only interrupt occasionally to correct some pedantic detail or other.
You tell Elek about travelling into the Abyss to the coordinates, to the rogue planet. Elek nods along, fascinated enough to only interrupt occasionally about some phenomenon or other.

He goes quiet when you get to the Onslaught Mk.I - and begins shaking his head as you describe the Threat.

"No, this is terribly unlikely," he says. "The imaginings of some absurd holo-novel. Which of my students put you up to this jape?"
"Excellent," says Elek, confirming the transmission request with a tap. "Tell me, what did you find? What's behind all the excitement 200 cycles ago?"
Elek turns his attention to the datapad. "It's coming through," he says, confirming the transmission request with a tap.
Elek turns his attention to his datapad. "It's coming through," he says, confirming the transmission request with a tap.
You tell Elek about finding the sensor array, processing the data, then travelling into the Abyss. Elek nods along, fascinated enough to only interrupt occasionally about some phenomenon or other.
He goes quiet when you get to the Onslaught Mk.I - and begins shaking his head as you describe the Threat.
"No, this is terribly unlikely" he says. "The imaginings of some absurd holo-novel. Which of my students put you up to this jape?"
Elek gives an amused huff, as if at a student giving an excuse for not completing coursework by his deadline.
"I, I don't see how this can be," he says. "It's like the imaginings of some absurd holo-novel. If, if it were true, my patron... the provost, Hegemony COMSEC..."
He gives you an unconvinced look. "I'm not angry, I'm... disappointed," he says.

Elek gives an amused huff, as if at student giving an excuse for not completing coursework by his deadline.

"I'm not angry," he says. "I'm disappointed."

"I'm not angry," he says. "I'm disappointed. That's your story? I'd need some very good data indeed if I am to believe a word of it."

He taps his datapad, opening a stream for you, then fixes you with a skeptical glare.

"I say, $playerSirOrMadam - prove yourself."

Elek begins shuffling through your data, accessing his larger holodisplay with his datapad. Images, charts, holoclips start appearing around him. You watch his face turn from exasperated skepticism to simply fearful.

He slaps his datapad, and the holos disappear.

He turns to you, struggling to maintain his composure. "Th-thank you captain, for-"

He touches his forehead. "Your hazard pay!"

Elek remembered. He must be truly out of sorts.
He touches his forehead. "Your hazard pay!"
"If..." He gives you an odd look. "If you say so."
He touches his forehead. "Your payment!"

"I... I suppose it is."

Elek briefly attempts a sad smile before giving up.
With trembling hand, he taps at his datapad. He looks relieved when the payment confirms - your TriPad gives a corresponding satisfied chirp.
"There. We can put this all... behind us. I'll handle it. My patron... it's going to be fine." He manages a sickly smile.

He lets out an upset noise, but no objection as he taps again at his datapad, hands shaking. He has to perform the command twice before getting it right.

"Yes... there. Good-day, captain. Please keep this... I'll take care of everything."

He lets out an upset noise, but no objection as he taps again at his datapad, hands shaking. He has to perform the command twice before getting it right.

"Yes... there. Now. Tell me about your discovery. I've certainly paid dearly for it."

He looks sick, the affect of the confident academic completely shot.

Perhaps there is some knowledge that the academician would have been happier to have never learned.

Elek cuts the comms.

He looks sick, the affect of the confident academic completely shot. Elek sits down at his desk to stare at his blank datapad.

Ignoring you.
